1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide __and at least one enzyme encapsulated within the compartment, wherein the enzyme is not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in the same cell type__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __and the at least one enzyme is functionally localized within the compartment__.

3. (Original) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme.

4. (Original) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __that directs localization of the enzyme to the interior of the non-native compartment__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __derived from a non-native source relative to the host cell__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and at least one additional Eut shell protein__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __from at least two different BMC operons or bacterial species__.

9. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species.

10. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __for selective purification of the non-native compartment__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and at least one enzyme not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in the same cell type, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and the at least one enzyme, and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide __with the at least one enzyme encapsulated therein, wherein the compartment catalyzes a metabolic reaction not naturally catalyzed by the host cell__.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and the polynucleotide encodes heterologous BMC polypeptides not naturally present in the Shewanellaceae host__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the polynucleotide encodes heterologous BMC polypeptides not naturally present in yeast__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae __and the BMC polypeptides are derived from a bacterial source__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae __and the non-native compartment is functional in the yeast host__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the polynucleotide encodes heterologous BMC polypeptides not naturally present in the alga__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product __not naturally produced by the host cell__; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __within the non-native compartment__.

22. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product.

23. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor.

24. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production.

25. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate.

26. (Original) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __wherein each compartment independently comprises at least one BMC polypeptide__.
